propositions: When a provider-qualified primary model escalates on a context limit error with no model-class table configured, _rung_target silently drops the provider qualifier and returns a bare Anthropic model id, causing the pass-1 retry to execute on an unintended provider (e.g. Bedrock primary escalates to direct Anthropic).

The rung target decision in _rung_target compares class resolution against inferred provider form but never receives the run's actual primary model as input, making the decision derivable only from module constants.

Pass-1 entry rung named 'frontier' resolves to an Anthropic model, so models_at_or_above returns bare model ids even on the common one-criterion retry before any escalation is needed, not confined to rare deep-escalation cases.

When a model-class table IS configured for another provider, models_at_or_above correctly returns provider-qualified escalation targets, but the unconfigured-table plus provider-qualified primary combination has no test coverage and fails.

Escalation to an unnameable higher rung (one that cannot be expressed in the run's provider because the class vocabulary is not configured) should fail safe with a visible too-big failure finding, not silently cross to a different provider.
